mainTopic: Flawed גיטין: what happens after the fact, the הלכה like רבי אלעזר, and גיטין for several couples
overview: Our משנה lists flawed גיטין, such as one signed by only one witness. רב says a single-witness גט leaves the child כשר only if the husband wrote it himself. שמואל says even a סופר's handwriting is enough, and each answers the other's proof from a later משנה. רב rules that a woman who remarried with one of these flawed גיטין stays with her second husband only if she has children. The גמרא defends this against a challenge from יבמות by explaining that the flaw is only a rabbinic concern. לוי and רבי יוחנן say she never has to leave, and along the way the גמרא discusses whether a קרצית disqualifies מי חטאת. Many reports then confirm that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, who validates a גט handed over before witnesses. A new משנה follows about mixed-up identical גיטין and about one גט written for five couples. The גמרא debates whether that משנה fits רבי אלעזר, and then defines a shared wording versus separate formulas. רבי יוחנן's answer is given, and ריש לקיש's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: רב limits the case to the husband's own handwriting
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's lenient outcome (child is כשר) applies only when the גט is in the husband's handwriting plus one witness, not in a סופר's handwriting plus one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when the גט is in his own handwriting with one witness. But if it is in a scribe's handwriting with one witness, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains which גט our משנה means when it says a גט with only one witness is פסול but the child is still כשר. He says it must be written in the husband's own handwriting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's own handwriting adds strength to a גט that has only one witness. A סופר's handwriting adds nothing of the husband's, so in that case the גט is fully invalid and the child is not כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically; only in this case
His own handwriting (the husband's)
A scribe's handwriting
A witness (here, only one signed)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is saying this גט is good to use from the start. The question is only what happens after the fact, if she already remarried and had a child.

phrases.english: And specifically his handwriting and one witness;
but a scribe's handwriting and one witness – no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case of the משנה (one witness, child כשר).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a גט in the husband's handwriting with one witness makes the child כשר בדיעבד. A סופר's handwriting with one witness does not.

steps.title: שמואל includes a scribe's handwriting too
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב: even a גט in a סופר's handwriting with one witness falls under the משנה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: even a scribe's handwriting with one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his opposing view. He holds that a סופר's handwriting with one witness is also enough for the child to be כשר. He is about to bring his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב, שמואל does not need the husband's own handwriting. A סופר-written גט with one witness has the same after-the-fact status.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
even a scribe's handwriting and one witness,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ כְּתַב סוֹפֵר וְעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב's limitation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a סופר-written גט with one witness makes the child כשר בדיעבד.

steps.title: שמואל's proof from another משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל cites a משנה (87b) that says a גט in a סופר's handwriting with one witness is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we learned: a scribe's handwriting and one witness is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל backs up his view with a משנה that explicitly calls a סופר-written גט with one witness כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another משנה calls this exact combination כשר, then surely our משנה's weaker after-the-fact ruling also covers it. That means רב's limit to the husband's handwriting is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: For we have learned (in a משנה)
Valid

phrases.english: as we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה found later, on 87b.

phrases.english: a scribe's handwriting and one witness – valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for שמואל's statement.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a סופר's handwriting with one witness qualifies
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 87b: כתב סופר ועד – כשר

steps.title: רב: the two משניות are not comparable
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects the proof. The other משנה lets her marry לכתחילה, so it must be a stronger case. Our משנה is only בדיעבד, so it is a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב would say: is it comparable? There she may marry from the start. Here it is only after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב would push back on שמואל's proof. The two משניות have different outcomes, so they cannot describe the same גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 87b משנה the גט is fully good, so she may remarry from the start. רב understands that one as a case where the סופר also signed as the second witness. Our משנה only saves the child after the fact, so it must be a weaker גט: the husband's handwriting with one witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable?
From the start; allowed up front
After the fact
She may marry

phrases.english: And Rav: is it comparable?!
There, she may marry from the start;
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה on 87b, where the גט is fully valid.

phrases.english: here, only after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב against שמואל's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from 87b, but not that משנה's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two משניות have different outcomes (לכתחילה vs. בדיעבד), so they cannot describe the same case.

steps.title: שמואל: expert scribe versus non-expert scribe
steps.stepSummary: שמואל keeps both משניות about a סופר-written גט with one witness. The 87b משנה speaks of an expert סופר, so it is fully valid. Our משנה speaks of a non-expert סופר, so it is only good after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל would say: it is not difficult. This one is an expert scribe, and that one is a scribe who is not expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how שמואל answers the difference רב pointed out. Both משניות are about a סופר's handwriting; the difference is how reliable the סופר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An expert סופר can be trusted to have written the גט properly on the husband's instructions, so she may remarry from the start. A non-expert סופר is less reliable, so with only one witness the גט is פסול, but the child is still כשר after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Scribe (Aramaic)
Expert; well-known and reliable

steps.whatToRemember: רב: our משנה means the husband's handwriting plus one witness, and the 87b משנה has the סופר signing as the second witness. שמואל: both mean a סופר's handwriting plus one witness. If the סופר is an expert, she may marry from the start; if not, the child is only כשר after the fact.

phrases.english: And Shmuel: it is not difficult;
this one is with an expert scribe,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the משנה on 87b, where she may marry from the start.

phrases.english: and that one is with a scribe who is not expert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difference רב raised between the two משניות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): expert vs. non-expert סופר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the two משניות have different outcomes, it seemed they could not both describe a סופר-written גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both describe a סופר-written גט with one witness. The סופר's expertise decides whether it is good from the start or only after the fact.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement between רב and שמואל stands, and each can explain both משניות his own way.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees: the case is the husband's handwriting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the same thing as רב: the משנה is talking about a גט in the husband's own handwriting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too said רבי יוחנן: We learned "his handwriting."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן, who backs up רב's reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 1, רב limited the משנה to a גט in the husband's handwriting plus one witness. Now רבי יוחנן says the same thing, so רב is not alone. This also sets up a question from רבי אלעזר in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His handwriting, here meaning the husband wrote the גט himself
We learned, a way of saying 'this is what the משנה means'
And so too, which shows agreement with the opinion just said

phrases.english: And so too said Rabbi Yochanan:
We learned "his handwriting."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an agreeing voice to רב's reading from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's case is a גט in the husband's own handwriting.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks: that case already has witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר challenges רבי יוחנן: the גט you are talking about already has witnesses, so why does handwriting matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to him: But there are witnesses on it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר pushes back on רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר understood רבי יוחנן to be explaining the middle case of the משנה, a גט that has witnesses but no date. If it already has witnesses, the husband's handwriting adds nothing. So the statement seems pointless there.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to point out something obvious
Witnesses who sign the גט

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to him:
But there are witnesses on it!
phrases.notes: He thought רבי יוחנן meant the middle case of the משנה, which already has witnesses signed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲרֵי יֵשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the משנה means 'his handwriting'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is the middle clause, the גט already has witnesses, so requiring the husband's handwriting adds nothing.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: I meant the last clause
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he was talking about the last clause of the משנה, where there is only one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On the last clause.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן clears up the misunderstanding. He was explaining the last case, not the middle one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last case of the משנה has only one witness, so the husband's handwriting really does matter there. This matches רב exactly: husband's handwriting plus one witness. רבי אלעזר's question only worked because he applied the statement to the wrong clause.

keyTerms.meaning: On the last clause, meaning the final case in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and רבי יוחנן say the משנה's last case is a גט in the husband's handwriting with one witness.

phrases.english: He said to him: On the last clause.
phrases.notes: That last case is the one with only one witness, so the husband's handwriting is what makes it work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's challenge from step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-locating the statement to a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was explaining the middle clause, which already has witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was explaining the last clause, where there is only one witness.

steps.title: Two opposite rulings from רב
steps.stepSummary: רב is reported to have said both that the woman must leave her second husband and that she need not leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes רב said: She must leave. Sometimes רב said: She need not leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic and points out that רב seems to contradict himself. This sets up the resolution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who remarried using one of the משנה's three flawed גיטין. The משנה said the child is כשר, but it did not say whether she may stay with her new husband. רב is quoted both ways, and the גמרא needs to explain how.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
She must leave her second husband
She need not leave her second husband

phrases.english: Sometimes Rav said: She must leave,
phrases.notes: This is about a woman who remarried using one of the משנה's three flawed גיטין.

phrases.english: sometimes Rav said: She need not leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין אָמַר רַב: תֵּצֵא, זִימְנִין אָמַר רַב: לֹא תֵּצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the משנה's three flawed גיטין
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rulings about a woman who remarried with a flawed גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב gave two opposite rulings for what looks like the same case.

steps.title: It depends on whether she has children
steps.stepSummary: The two rulings of רב are about two different cases: if she has children she stays, and if she has none she must leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If she has children, she need not leave. If she has no children, she must leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רב's contradiction by splitting it into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ruling of רב applies to a different situation. Whether she already has children from the second husband is what makes the difference. The גמרא does not spell out the reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? A phrase used to set up a way of fitting two statements together
Children

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a woman who remarried with one of these flawed גיטין stays if she has children and leaves if she has none.

phrases.english: How so?
If she has children, she need not leave,
phrases.notes: He means children from her second husband.

phrases.english: if she has no children, she must leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב gave opposite rulings for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: With children she stays. Without children she leaves.

steps.title: מר זוטרא בר טוביה begins an objection from יבמות
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בר טוביה starts to challenge רב by quoting a משנה about doubtful marriage or divorce in the laws of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בר טוביה raises an objection: And all of them who had a doubtful betrothal or a doubtful divorce, these do חליצה and do not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא בר טוביה opens a challenge against רב by quoting a משנה. Here he is setting up the source, and the actual objection comes in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted משנה deals with the fifteen forbidden relatives whose co-wives are normally freed from יבום. If the forbidden relative's marriage or divorce with the dead brother was only doubtful, her co-wives must do חליצה and may not do יבום. Quoting a source that treats a doubtful divorce strictly lays the groundwork for challenging רב's lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
A betrothal whose validity is in doubt
A divorce whose validity is in doubt
They do חליצה, the ceremony that frees a widow from יבום
They marry the dead husband's brother through יבום

phrases.english: Mar Zutra bar Toviya raises an objection:
And all of them,
phrases.notes: This quotes a משנה in יבמות 30b about the fifteen forbidden relatives whose co-wives are freed from יבום.

phrases.english: who had a doubtful betrothal
or a doubtful divorce,
these perform חליצה and do not do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an objection to רב's ruling from step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's lenient ruling about a woman who remarried with a flawed גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only so far: the quoted משנה treats a doubtful divorce strictly. The full attack is stated in step 14.

steps.title: Defining a doubtful betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source explains what a ספק קידושין is: he threw the betrothal to her, and it is unclear whether it landed closer to her or closer to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a doubtful betrothal? He threw the betrothal money to her, and it may have landed closer to her or closer to him. That is a doubtful betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא בר טוביה keeps quoting the source he started in Step 11. Here it defines the first case, a doubtful betrothal, to set up his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Betrothal works only if the woman actually acquires the item. If nobody knows whether it landed closer to her or closer to him, nobody knows whether she is married. This case is background; the important case for our סוגיא comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal whose validity is uncertain
He threw
Closer to her, so she acquires it
Closer to him, so she does not acquire it

phrases.english: How is there a doubtful betrothal?
If he threw the betrothal to her,
and it is possibly closer to her,
and possibly closer to him,
this is a doubtful betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source quoted in Step 11 by defining its first term.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothal thrown to a woman that may have landed closer to either side is a ספק קידושין.

steps.title: Defining a doubtful divorce: the three flawed גיטין
steps.stepSummary: The source defines ספק גירושין using the three flawed גיטין of our משנה: written by the husband with no witnesses, witnesses but no date, or a date but only one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: A doubtful divorce: he wrote it in his own handwriting with no witnesses on it; or it has witnesses but no date; or it has a date but only one witness. These are doubtful divorces.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted source now defines a doubtful divorce. It names exactly the three flawed גיטין from our משנה, which is why מר זוטרא is bringing it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the link that drives the challenge. The source treats our משנה's three גיטין as only a 'doubtful' divorce. So the woman's divorce from her first husband is not clearly finished.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorce whose validity is uncertain
His own handwriting
The date written in the גט
A single witness

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same flawed גיטין we have been discussing have consequences in the laws of יבום, not only for the woman herself.

phrases.english: A doubtful divorce:
he wrote it in his own handwriting
and there are no witnesses on it;

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים וְאֵין בּוֹ זְמַן,
phrases.english: there are witnesses on it but no date in it;
there is a date in it
but it has only one witness —
this is a doubtful divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְפֵק גֵּירוּשִׁין כָּתַב בִּכְתַב יָדוֹ וְאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted source with its second definition, the one that matches our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three flawed גיטין of our משנה make up a ספק גירושין.

steps.title: If she stays married, her co-wife will do יבום
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא completes his challenge: if רב lets her stay with her second husband, people will treat her divorce as complete, and her צרה will come to do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say she need not leave, then her co-wife will come to do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the actual challenge to רב comes out. If the woman keeps her second husband, her co-wife will wrongly be allowed to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted source treats this divorce as doubtful, so the co-wife may not do יבום. But if רב lets the woman stay with her second husband, it looks as though the divorce is fully valid. Then the co-wife will come to do יבום, against that source.

keyTerms.meaning: Her co-wife, the first husband's other wife
To do יבום, marrying the dead husband's brother
She need not leave her second husband

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is about the co-wife, not the woman with the flawed גט. Her staying married would make people think the first marriage was fully ended.

phrases.english: And if you say she need not leave,
her co-wife will come to do יבום!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the quoted source's definition of ספק גירושין to attack רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling (Step 10) that a woman with children need not leave her second husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source treats these גיטין as a doubtful divorce, so the co-wife may not do יבום. Letting the woman stay implies a complete divorce, which would lead the co-wife to do יבום.

steps.title: The co-wife may do יבום, because the concern is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the co-wife may indeed do יבום. The flaw in the גט is only a חששא דרבנן; by תורה law, the divorce is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her do יבום, and there is nothing wrong with that. It is only a rabbinic concern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by accepting the result. Yes, the co-wife may do יבום, and that is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the divorce was truly in doubt. The answer is that by תורה law the גט works, and the doubt is only a rabbinic worry. So the co-wife is permitted to do יבום, and רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Let her do יבום
There is nothing wrong with it
A concern only by rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: The three flawed גיטין of our משנה are valid by תורה law. Their problem is only מדרבנן, so a co-wife can do יבום and רב's ruling holds.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the level of the problem. These flawed גיטין are a rabbinic issue, not a תורה-level doubt.

phrases.english: Let her do יבום, and there is nothing wrong with that;
it is only a rabbinic concern.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14 by accepting its result.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the outcome and lowers the level of the problem: the flaw is rabbinic, not from the תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The divorce is truly doubtful, so the co-wife's יבום would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט is valid by תורה law and the concern is only rabbinic, so the co-wife may do יבום.

steps.title: לוי and רבי יוחנן: she never has to leave
steps.stepSummary: לוי and רבי יוחנן rule that a woman who remarried with one of the flawed גיטין never has to leave her second husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said: She never has to leave. And רבי יוחנן said the same: She never has to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion that disagrees with רב. לוי and רבי יוחנן say the woman stays with her second husband no matter what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said she must leave unless she already had children (step 10). לוי and רבי יוחנן go further: she never leaves, children or not. The גמרא gives no reason for their view here.

keyTerms.meaning: Never / in every case
She does not have to leave (her second husband)
An early אמורא, a colleague of רב

phrases.english: Levi said:
She never has to leave.
And so said Rabbi Yochanan:
She never has to leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion that argues with רב's ruling discussed in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who remarried with one of the משנה's flawed גיטין never has to leave her second husband.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי חלפתא's two teachings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the sons of רבי חלפתא that their father taught both that she never leaves and that a קרצית does not disqualify מי חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן also said to the sons of רבי חלפתא from הונא: This is what your father said: She never has to leave. And a קרצית in the sheaf does not disqualify מי חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן supports his ruling by saying he heard it from an earlier teacher, רבי חלפתא. Along with it, he passes on a second, unrelated teaching from the same teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first teaching backs up the ruling of step 16 with an older source. The second teaching is about מי חטאת: if a קרצית drinks from this water, the water is still usable. The גמרא now turns to explain and test this second teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A small creature found in the sheaves (defined in step 19)
Sheaf / bundle of cut grain
Purification water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
Makes invalid / disqualifies
Your father

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Yochanan said to them,
to the sons of Rabbi Chalafta from Huna,
This is what your father said:
She never has to leave;
and a kartzit that is in the sheaf
does not disqualify the water of purification.
phrases.notes: Even if it drinks from this water, the water can still be used. See במדבר 19:17–19.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לִבְנֵי רַבִּי חֲלַפְתָּא דְּמִן הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's ruling with an earlier authority and adds a second teaching from that authority.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that she never has to leave her second husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי חלפתא, as reported by רבי יוחנן to his sons.

steps.title: What is a קרצית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a קרצית is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a קרצית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask the meaning of an unusual word from רבי חלפתא's teaching. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the ruling about מי חטאת can be understood, we need to know what creature is being discussed. This is a simple word-clarifying question, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?

phrases.english: What is a kartzit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term in the second teaching of step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the creature called a קרצית.

steps.title: אביי: a fly found between the sheaves
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a קרצית is a type of fly found between the sheaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a fly found between the sheaves.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question: a קרצית is a kind of fly that lives among the sheaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the ruling is about a small flying creature. This matters for the next step, which compares the קרצית to birds that drink from מי חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא in בבל
A fly
Sheaves / bundles

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A fly that is found between the sheaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קרצית is a type of fly found between the sheaves.

steps.title: רב דניאל quotes a משנה: only the pigeon is excluded
steps.stepSummary: רב דניאל בר רב קטינא begins a challenge by quoting a משנה: all birds disqualify מי חטאת except the pigeon, because it sucks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דניאל בר רב קטינא raised an objection: All birds disqualify מי חטאת, except for the pigeon, because it sucks the water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דניאל starts to challenge the קרצית ruling by quoting a משנה. This sets up his point in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when any bird drinks from מי חטאת, the water becomes invalid. The only exception it lists is the pigeon, because of how it drinks. The fact that the קרצית is not listed is the basis for the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (from a source)
Birds / flying creatures
Pigeon / dove
Sucks (drinks by sucking)

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב דָּנִיאֵל בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Daniel bar Rav Ketina raised an objection:
All birds disqualify the water of purification,
except for the pigeon –
because it sucks.
phrases.notes: Other birds let water drip back from their beaks; the pigeon sucks it up, so nothing drips back in.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב דָּנִיאֵל בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the קרצית ruling, now that קרצית has been defined as a flying creature.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חלפתא's ruling that a קרצית does not disqualify מי חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה lists all flying creatures as disqualifying, with only the pigeon left out.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have listed the קרצית too
steps.stepSummary: If a קרצית really does not disqualify, the משנה should have said: except for the pigeon and the קרצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, let the משנה teach: except for the pigeon and the קרצית!
steps.whatsHappening: רב דניאל finishes his challenge. If the קרצית were also an exception, the משנה should have named it next to the pigeon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a complete list of exceptions, and only the pigeon is on it. Leaving out the קרצית suggests that it does disqualify the water, which goes against רבי חלפתא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so
Let it teach / it should have taught

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge is from silence: the משנה names only the pigeon as an exception, so a קרצית seems to disqualify מי חטאת.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if a קרצית really does not disqualify the water, as רבי חלפתא said.

phrases.english: let it teach: except for the pigeon and the kartzit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, נִיתְנֵי: חוּץ מִיּוֹנָה וְקַרְצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the point of the challenge from the משנה quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a קרצית does not disqualify מי חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists only the pigeon as an exception, so the קרצית must disqualify the water like all other flying creatures.

steps.title: Why the קרצית Is Not Listed: Big and Small Differ
steps.stepSummary: The משנה could not list the קרצית as an exception, because a big one does not disqualify while a small one does.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a clean, across-the-board rule: a big one does not disqualify, and a small one does disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב דניאל's question from Step 21: the משנה did not write 'except the pigeon and the קרצית' because the קרצית does not have one single rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה lists only exceptions that work every time. The pigeon never disqualifies, so it is listed. A big קרצית is fine but a small one disqualifies, so it could not be listed as a simple exception, and רבי חלפתא's teaching still stands for the big kind.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not clear-cut for him; there is no single rule
A large one (here: a big קרצית)
A small one
Disqualifies (the מי חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי חלפתא was wrong. His rule that a קרצית does not disqualify still holds, but only for a big one.

phrases.english: It is not clear-cut for him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the author of the משנה. He could not list the קרצית, because it does not fit one rule.

phrases.english: for a large one does not disqualify,
and a small one does disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the משנה lists only exceptions that apply every time, and the קרצית does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a קרצית never disqualifies, the משנה should have listed it next to the pigeon.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a big קרצית does not disqualify; a small one does, so the משנה could not list it as a simple exception.

steps.title: How Small Counts as Small?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks up to what size a קרצית is 'small' and disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to what size?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question to get the size limit between a 'small' and a 'big' קרצית. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know size matters, we need a line. The question asks where 'small' ends.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much? (asking for a measure)

phrases.english: And up to how much?
phrases.notes: He means: up to what size is a קרצית still 'small', so that it disqualifies?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the size measure behind the distinction in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size limit for a 'small' קרצית that disqualifies.

steps.title: Up to the Size of an Olive
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה (or רבי אמי) says: up to a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said, and some say it was רבי אמי: up to the size of an olive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the size: a קרצית up to a כזית counts as small and disqualifies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the line between the two cases from Step 22. The גמרא is not sure which אמורא said it, so it gives both names.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was said by someone else)
The size of an olive

steps.whatToRemember: A big קרצית does not disqualify מי חטאת; a small one, up to a כזית, does.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said,
and some say it was Rabbi Ami:
Up to an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קרצית up to a כזית is 'small' and disqualifies.

steps.title: רב Rules Like רבי אלעזר for גיטין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר from the משנה, and רב rules like him for bills of divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי אלעזר says: Even if, etc.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר for גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה: רבי אלעזר's view, and רב's ruling that the הלכה follows him for גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that a גט works even with no witnesses signed on it, as long as it was handed over in front of witnesses. רב accepts this, but he says it only for גיטין, which sets up שמואל's addition next.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote from the משנה
The הלכה follows (this opinion)
Bills of divorce

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Even if, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: even with no witnesses signed, if he gave it to her in front of witnesses, the גט works.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Elazar with regard to bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל פִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, leaving the קרצית discussion behind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר for גיטין.

steps.title: שמואל: Also for Money Documents
steps.stepSummary: When רב יהודה told this to שמואל, שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר for money documents too.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said: Also for documents.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports that שמואל goes further than רב: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר for שטרות as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two views. רב applies רבי אלעזר only to גיטין, while שמואל applies him to money documents too, like loan papers.

keyTerms.meaning: When I said it before him
Documents, here money documents like loan papers

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, telling over רב's ruling to שמואל.

phrases.english: he said: Also with regard to documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רב's ruling from Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר for money documents too.

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר Spoke About Collecting Money
steps.stepSummary: How can רב say the הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר for documents, when רבי אלעזר taught that she collects from sold property?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רב hold that for documents it is not so?! But it teaches: 'and she collects from liened property'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב: רבי אלעזר's own words in the משנה deal with money, so how can רב limit him to גיטין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that with this גט she can collect her כתובה even from property the husband already sold, a money matter. So רבי אלעזר clearly spoke about money too, and רב seems to cut his view in half.

keyTerms.meaning: And does רב hold...?
But it teaches! (pointing to a source)
Liened property: land the debtor sold that is still tied to his debt
Collects (money owed)

phrases.english: And does Rav hold
that with regard to documents it is not so?!
But it teaches:
And she collects from liened property!
phrases.notes: She collects her כתובה with this גט, even from land he sold. That is a money matter, not just divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's limit from Step 25 using the משנה's own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר only for גיטין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר himself mentioned collecting from sold property, a money ruling. So his view covers documents, and רב should not split it.

steps.title: Two Rulings: רב Takes One
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר made two separate rulings; רב agrees with the divorce one and disagrees with the money one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said two things; רב agrees with him on one and disagrees with him on one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבי אלעזר's statement holds two separate rulings, and רב is allowed to follow one without the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ruling is that the גט works for divorce; the other is that it works as a money document to collect from sold property. These are separate, so רב follows רבי אלעזר on divorce and argues with him on money. שמואל follows him on both.

keyTerms.meaning: He said two things
Like him (agrees with his view)
On one (point)
Disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: רב: follow רבי אלעזר only for גיטין. שמואל: follow him for גיטין and money documents. An אמורא can accept one part of a תנא's view and reject another.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one line in a משנה can hold more than one ruling, and a later authority can decide each one separately.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said two things;
and Rav holds like him in one,
and disagrees with him in one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting a statement into two separate rulings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's view is one package, so רב must accept it for documents too.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר made two rulings; רב accepts the divorce ruling and rejects the money ruling.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי also rules like רבי אלעזר for a גט
steps.stepSummary: Another report: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר regarding a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר regarding a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more אמורא who agrees with רב: for a גט, the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב ruled like רבי אלעזר for a גט. Now רבי יהושע בן לוי is quoted saying the same thing, which gives רב's ruling more support.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly. It brings another source that says the same thing.
The final ruling follows this opinion.
Bills of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי
phrases.english: And similarly, Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another אמורא who supports רב's ruling in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר for a גט.

steps.title: רבי ינאי says it doesn't even have the scent of a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי says this גט does not have even a trace of a real גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ינאי said: it doesn't even have the scent of a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: Right next to that ruling, the גמרא quotes רבי ינאי, who seems to say the opposite. He says this document is worth nothing as a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not even the scent of a גט' means the document counts for nothing at all. It sounds like רבי ינאי totally rejects רבי אלעזר. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'scent' of a גט: even a small trace or partial effect of a divorce.
It does not have in it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yannai said:
It does not have even the scent of a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ רֵיחַ הַגֵּט אֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a statement that seems to oppose step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This גט has no validity at all, not even a trace.

steps.title: Does רבי ינאי reject רבי אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in surprise: does רבי ינאי really not accept רבי אלעזר's view?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי ינאי not hold like רבי אלעזר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised. It asks whether רבי ינאי really disagrees with רבי אלעזר, when so many other אמוראים follow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is aimed at the strong words of רבי ינאי. If he means the גט is worthless, he would stand alone against everyone who rules like רבי אלעזר. The phrasing is a question, but it works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it; he does not accept that view.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר?!
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yannai not hold like Rabbi Elazar?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how to read step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling the גט worthless seems to reject רבי אלעזר outright, against the other אמוראים who rule like him.

steps.title: רבי ינאי was speaking according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי meant that according to the רבנן, who argue with רבי אלעזר, this גט has no trace of validity.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: according to the רבנן, it doesn't even have the scent of a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי ינאי was not giving his own ruling. He was describing the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי was explaining how far the opposing view goes: for the רבנן, the document is completely worthless. This does not tell us that he rules like them, so he may still agree that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It reinterprets a statement.
The Sages who disagree with רבי אלעזר in the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'not even the scent of a גט' as רבי ינאי's own final ruling. He is only describing the view of the רבנן.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying: according to the Rabbis,
it does not have even the scent of a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the statement describes another opinion, not his own ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ינאי rejects רבי אלעזר and says the גט is worthless.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ינאי only described the view of the רבנן. He does not necessarily disagree with ruling like רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: ריש לקיש also rules like רבי אלעזר for a גט
steps.stepSummary: Another report: ריש לקיש says the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר regarding a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of ריש לקיש: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר regarding a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, matching pair of reports. It starts with ריש לקיש, who also rules like רבי אלעזר for a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the same pattern as steps 29-30, but with different אמוראים. It adds ריש לקיש to the list of supporters of רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי שמעון בן לקיש, a leading אמורא in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: And similarly, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said
that Reish Lakish said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second pair of reports with the same pattern as step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר for a גט.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says it doesn't even have the scent of a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses the same strong words as רבי ינאי: this גט has no trace of validity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: it doesn't even have the scent of a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like before, the גמרא quotes a second אמורא, רבי יוחנן, who seems to say the opposite. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same words רבי ינאי used. Again, it sounds like a full rejection of רבי אלעזר, this time from רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The great אמורא of ארץ ישראל, and the main partner in debate of ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
It does not have even the scent of a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ רֵיחַ הַגֵּט אֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a statement that seems to oppose step 33, just like step 30 did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This גט has no validity at all, not even a trace.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן reject רבי אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: should we say רבי יוחנן does not accept רבי אלעזר's view?
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say רבי יוחנן does not hold like רבי אלעזר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked about רבי ינאי: does רבי יוחנן really reject רבי אלעזר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'not even the scent of a גט' seem to throw out רבי אלעזר's view completely. The גמרא challenges whether that is really what רבי יוחנן means.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It suggests a possible reading that the גמרא will test.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר?!
phrases.english: Shall we say Rabbi Yochanan does not hold like Rabbi Elazar?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how to read step 34, the same way step 31 challenged step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling the גט worthless seems to reject רבי אלעזר outright, against ריש לקיש and the others.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was also speaking according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Like רבי ינאי, רבי יוחנן only meant that according to the רבנן, this גט has no trace of validity.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: according to the רבנן, it doesn't even have the scent of a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. רבי יוחנן was describing the view of the רבנן, not giving his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, there is no real argument between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן. One gives the practical הלכה (like רבי אלעזר), and the other explains how completely the רבנן reject this גט.
steps.whatToRemember: Many אמוראים (רב, שמואל, רבי יהושע בן לוי, ריש לקיש) rule like רבי אלעזר for a גט. 'Not even the scent of a גט' only describes the view of the רבנן, so it does not argue with that ruling.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying: according to the Rabbis,
it does not have even the scent of a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35 with the same answer given in step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the statement describes another opinion, not his own ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן rejects רבי אלעזר and says the גט is worthless.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן only described the view of the רבנן. He does not necessarily disagree with ruling like רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: A question is sent to רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא sends a message through מרי בר מר asking רב הונא whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר זבדא sent to מרי בר מר: Ask רב הונא whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר regarding a גט or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which a real question is sent to a great teacher: does the הלכה follow רבי אלעזר in גיטין? This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps just before this already brought reports and questions about whether the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר. Now the גמרא shows that this was a live question that people sent to the leading teacher of the generation.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him (a message)
Ask of him; request an answer from him
Bills of divorce
The final ruling follows (someone's opinion)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda sent
to Marei bar Mar:
Ask Rav Huna:
Is the halacha like Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce,
or is it not the halacha?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא לְמָרִי בַּר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן do not reject רבי אלעזר, the גמרא brings more sources on the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practical הלכה in גיטין follows רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: רב הונא dies, and his son רבה answers
steps.stepSummary: Before the question arrives, רב הונא passes away. His son רבה answers in his father's name: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile רב הונא died. His son רבה said to him: This is what my father said in the name of רבא: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר regarding a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The question reaches רב הונא's house too late, because he has died. His son רבה answers using a teaching he heard from his father: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer still carries רב הונא's authority, because רבה is repeating what his father taught. The question from step 37 now gets a clear yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile; in the meantime
He passed away (literally, his soul rested)
His son
In the name of...

phrases.english: Meanwhile, Rav Huna passed away.
Rabba, his son, said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is מרי בר מר, the one who brought the question.

phrases.english: This is what my father said in the name of Rava:
The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question sent in step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין, as רב הונא taught.

steps.title: The tradition is traced back to רב
steps.stepSummary: רבה adds that the experts reported the same ruling from 'our teacher' רב, through רב חמא בר גוריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our teachers who are experts in הלכה said in the name of our teacher: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין. This refers to what רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה strengthens his answer by showing that the ruling goes all the way back to רב. The גמרא then explains who 'our teachers' and 'our teacher' are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Our teachers' means רב חמא בר גוריא, and 'our teacher' means רב. So the ruling does not rest only on רב הונא; it is an old tradition from רב himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teachers
Those who are expert in matters of הלכה
Our teacher (here, רב)

phrases.english: And our teachers who are experts in matters of halacha
said in the name of our teacher:
The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
phrases.notes: This line tells us who is meant: "our teachers" is רב חמא בר גוריא, and "our teacher" is רב.

phrases.english: The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ הַבְּקִיאִין בִּדְבַר הֲלָכָה מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further source backing the answer given in step 38.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חמא בר גוריא reporting in the name of רב.

steps.title: A second version of the chain from רב
steps.stepSummary: Another version says the reporters were 'our colleagues and our teacher's students', meaning רב חסדא, who reported from רב חמא בר גוריא in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Our colleagues who are experts in הלכה, the students of our teacher, said in the name of our teacher: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין. This refers to what רב חסדא said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא, in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבה's words. The chain of names is a little different, but the ruling is the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version 'our colleagues' is רב חסדא, who was רבה's colleague, and he adds one more link: רב חסדא from רב חמא בר גוריא from רב. The two versions argue only about who passed the tradition along, not about the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (a different version)
Our colleagues
The students of our teacher

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this is a new opinion. Both versions agree the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר; only the chain of names is different.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
And our colleagues who are experts in matters of halacha,
and the students of our teacher,
said in the name of our teacher:
The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Chisda said that Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the chain of tradition reported in step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין, through רב חסדא from רב חמא בר גוריא from רב.

steps.title: רבין brings the same ruling from ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he reported that רבי אלעזר the אמורא said in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, when רבין came, he said that רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more report, this time from ארץ ישראל, and it agrees with everything before it. The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the report brought from ארץ ישראל goes back to רב with the same ruling. So the reports from both places agree.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise
When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people called רבי אלעזר here. The one reporting from רב is a later אמורא; the one whose opinion is the הלכה is the earlier תנא.
steps.whatToRemember: Every report agrees: רב הונא, רב through רב חמא בר גוריא (in both versions), and רבין's report all say the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.whyThisMatters: So many separate chains agree that this ruling is solid and practical, not just one person's view.

phrases.english: And likewise, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Elazar said that Rav said:
phrases.notes: This רבי אלעזר is the later אמורא, a student of רב, not the תנא whose opinion we are deciding.

phrases.english: The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a matching report from ארץ ישראל to the Babylonian chains in steps 38-40.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report: רבי אלעזר the אמורא in the name of רב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין.

steps.title: Two identical גיטין that got mixed up
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when two identical גיטין are mixed up, the שליח gives both to each wife. So if one is lost, the other is useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two men sent their wives identical גיטין, and the גיטין got mixed up. The שליח gives both to this wife and both to that wife. So if one of them was lost, the remaining one is void.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a case of two identical גיטין that got mixed up. It tells the שליח to give both to each wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither גט can be told apart from the other, so the שליח cannot know which belongs to which wife. Handing both to each wife makes sure each one receives her own גט. That is also why losing one ruins the other: you can no longer be sure the remaining one is the right one for either woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
Identical bills of divorce, with the same names for husbands and wives
They got mixed up
Void, of no use

steps.confusionAlert: "Both to this one and both to that one" does not mean each wife keeps two גיטין. The שליח gives both to the first wife, then gives both to the second wife, so each one surely received her own.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Two men who sent their wives
two identical bills of divorce, and they got mixed up;
he gives both to this wife, and both to that wife.
Therefore, if one of them was lost,
the second one is void.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion about the הלכה following רבי אלעזר in גיטין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed-up identical גיטין are each given to both wives. If one is lost, the other is void.

steps.title: Five husbands share one גט with a single formula
steps.stepSummary: If five husbands write one shared גט naming every couple, and the witnesses sign at the bottom, the גט is valid for all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five men wrote a general wording in the גט: 'So-and-so divorces so-and-so, and so-and-so divorces so-and-so,' and the witnesses signed below. All of them are valid, and the גט is given to each and every wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new case: one shared גט written for five couples together, using one combined formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because all the couples are written into one single formula, the witnesses' signatures at the bottom cover every name. So one document divorces all five wives. It just has to be handed to each wife in turn.

keyTerms.meaning: A general, combined wording that includes everyone
So-and-so (man) / so-and-so (woman)
Valid

phrases.english: Five husbands who wrote a general wording in the bill of divorce:
"The man so-and-so divorces so-and-so,
and so-and-so divorces so-and-so,"
and the witnesses signed below;
all of them are valid,
and it must be given to each and every wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another case of several couples involved with the same גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One combined formula signed by witnesses at the bottom is valid for all the couples. It is handed to each wife.

steps.title: Separate formulas for each couple: only the one next to the witnesses works
steps.stepSummary: If each couple has its own separate formula and the witnesses sign only at the bottom, only the formula read together with the signatures is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was writing a separate formula for each and every couple, and the witnesses signed below, the one that is read together with the witnesses is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the contrasting case: each couple gets its own separate formula on the same sheet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With separate formulas, each section stands alone. The signatures at the bottom are read only with the last formula, the one just above them. Only that couple's גט is valid. The other formulas have no witnesses of their own.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the written formula of the גט for one couple
Are read together with it, meaning the formula directly above the signatures
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: One shared formula makes the גט valid for everyone. Separate formulas make it valid only for the couple whose section sits right above the witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה כּוֹתֵב טוֹפֶס לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: If he was writing a formula for each and every couple,
and the witnesses signed below;
the one with which the witnesses are read
phrases.notes: This is the formula written right above the signatures, so the names and the signatures read as one unit.

phrases.english: is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה כּוֹתֵב טוֹפֶס לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 43: separate formulas instead of one combined formula.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When each couple has a separate formula, only the formula read together with the witnesses' signatures is valid.

steps.title: Which תנא taught the mixed-up גיטין rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the first case of the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא is behind the משנה's ruling about handing both גיטין to each wife. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about identifying the source. Handing over a גט without knowing which one is which only works under certain views of how a גט takes effect. So the גמרא wants to know whose view fits.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Who is the תנא, meaning whose opinion is this

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Who is the tanna who taught this?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the first case, where both mixed-up גיטין are given to each wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the first case of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion the ruling about mixed-up גיטין follows.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the משנה cannot follow רבי אלעזר. For him the witnesses to the handing-over make the divorce work, and here they do not know which גט she is getting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is not like רבי אלעזר. If it were רבי אלעזר, since he says the witnesses to the handing-over effect the divorce, these witnesses do not know with which of the two גיטין she is being divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question. The משנה is not following רבי אלעזר, and he explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that the divorce takes effect through the witnesses who watch the גט being handed to the woman. In the mixed-up case, those witnesses cannot tell which of the two identical גיטין is hers, so their watching cannot make the divorce work. The משנה says the method does work, so it must follow a different view.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who watch the גט being handed to the woman
They cut off, meaning they make the divorce take effect
With which one of them

steps.whyThisMatters: The steps just before this said that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר in גיטין. Here רבי ירמיה claims that this משנה does not follow him. אביי disputes this in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.
For if it were Rabbi Elazar,
since he says the witnesses of the handing-over effect the divorce,
these witnesses do not know
with which one of them she is being divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר. Under his view, the witnesses to the handing-over must know which גט she is receiving, and in this case they do not.

steps.title: אביי: The משנה Can Follow רבי אלעזר After All
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues against רבי ירמיה. רבי אלעזר requires a גט to be written for her, but he does not require it to be handed over for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי אלעזר. Yes, רבי אלעזר requires the גט to be written for this particular woman. But does he also require it to be given for this particular woman? Of course not!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second answer to the question of whose view the משנה follows. He disagrees with רבי ירמיה and says it can fit רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה thought that for רבי אלעזר, the witnesses to the handing-over must know which גט she is getting. אביי splits the process in two. The writing must be done for her, and here it was. The handing-over does not need that kind of focus, so it does not matter that nobody knows which of the two papers is hers.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. This opens a defense showing the case fits a view that was just rejected.
Writing the גט specifically for this woman
Handing over the גט specifically for this woman
Does he require? Here it is a rhetorical question meaning 'he does not.'

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say the handing-over is unimportant for רבי אלעזר. It is still what makes the divorce work. It just does not need to be done 'for her sake' the way the writing does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key distinction for רבי אלעזר's view. The 'for her' requirement belongs to the writing, not to the moment of giving.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Elazar.
Say that Rabbi Elazar requires
writing for her sake;
does he require giving for her sake?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ירמיה's answer in step 46 and gives an alternative answer to the question in step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can follow רבי אלעזר, since he requires only the writing, not the giving, to be done for her sake.

steps.title: What Exactly Are a 'General Wording' and a 'Formula'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about five husbands and asks how a כלל differs from a טופס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Five husbands who wrote a general wording, and so on. What counts as a general wording, and what counts as a separate formula?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the five husbands from step 43 and step 44. It asks for a definition of the two cases, setting up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave opposite rulings. With a כלל, the גט works for everyone. With a טופס, only the last one works. But it never explained what physically makes a document one or the other, and the גמרא now wants that defined.

keyTerms.meaning: A general wording that covers all the couples together
A formula. Here, a separate text for each couple.
What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: Five who wrote a general wording, etc.
What is the case of a general wording,
what is the case of a formula?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי כְּלָל, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי טוֹפֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the mixed-up גיטין and opens a new discussion about the five-husbands case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical definition of a כלל versus a טופס in the five-couples case.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It Depends on the Date
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that one date for all the couples makes it a כלל, while a separate date for each couple makes it a טופס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If there is one date for all of them, that is a general wording. If there is a date for each and every one, that is a separate formula.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question by pointing to the date written in the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one date opens the document and all the couples are listed under it, it is one combined text, so the signatures at the bottom cover everyone. If each couple has its own date, each is a separate text. Then the signatures only attach to the last one, right next to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question asked in step 48.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One shared date makes a כלל. A separate date for each couple makes a טופס.

steps.title: ריש לקיש Begins His Own Definition
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש starts to give a different definition of כלל and טופס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is introducing ריש לקיש, who will give his own answer to the same question, and his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and' signals a second answer standing next to רבי יוחנן's. Expect ריש לקיש to define כלל and טופס by a different standard than the date.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
And (he) says. Introduces a parallel opinion.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second answer to the question of step 48, alongside רבי יוחנן's in step 49.
